questions.question: A list says: apple, apple, apple, apple, apple. That is 5 apples. How many apple pictures do you draw?
questions.explain: One picture for each apple: 5 apples means 5 pictures. It is easy to lose count and draw 4 or 6 instead.

questions.question: You have 7 crayons in your desk. How many crayon pictures do you draw?
questions.explain: One crayon gets one picture, so 7 crayons means 7 pictures. Count the list carefully before you start drawing.

questions.question: Sam picked berries at the park. He tallied them: a crossed group of 5 and 3 more marks. How many berry pictures does he draw?
questions.explain: The crossed group is 5, plus 3 more makes 8. Sam draws 8 berry pictures. A common trap is reading the crossed group as 4 or 6.

questions.question: A list has: duck, duck, duck, duck, duck, duck, duck, duck, duck. How many duck pictures do you draw?
questions.explain: Count the list one by one: there are 9 ducks, so 9 pictures. It is easy to stop at 8 or overshoot to 10.

questions.question: Leo tallied the cookies he baked: one crossed group of 5 and two single marks. How many cookie pictures does Leo draw?
questions.explain: The crossed group is 5, plus 2 more is 7. Leo draws 7 cookie pictures. Read the crossed group as 5, not 4 or 6.

questions.question: Anna has a list of 5 flowers and 4 bugs. She draws one picture for each thing. How many pictures does she draw in total?
questions.explain: Add the two groups: 5 + 4 = 9 pictures in total. One picture per thing, then add the rows together.

questions.question: Tom has 6 buttons. He draws 5 button pictures in his picture graph. What did Tom do wrong?
options: The row is the wrong one
questions.explain: One picture per button means 6 buttons need 6 pictures. Tom drew 5, so he is one picture short — he skipped a button.

questions.question: A table shows that Mia found 8 rocks. She draws one picture for each rock. How many rock pictures does she draw?
questions.explain: One rock, one picture, so 8 rocks need 8 pictures. Stopping at 7 leaves a rock out, and 4 puts two rocks in one picture.

questions.question: Ben's tally of the fish at the pond shows two crossed groups of 5. He draws one fish picture for each fish. How many fish pictures does he draw?
questions.explain: A crossed group means 5, so 5 and 5 make 10 fish and 10 pictures. Counting a crossed group as 4 gives 8, which is too few.

questions.question: Dan has 7 stamps. He puts one picture for each stamp in his graph. Which row is right?
questions.explain: Count the stamps, then draw that many pictures: 7 stamps, 7 pictures. The row with 4 pictures hides two stamps in one picture.

questions.question: Noah kept a tally of the buses that drove past his school. His tally shows three crossed groups of 5. He draws one bus picture for each bus. How many bus pictures does Noah draw?
questions.explain: Count the crossed groups by 5s: 5, 10, 15 buses, so 15 pictures. Counting each group as 4 gives 12 and loses three buses.

questions.question: Priya tallied the goals her soccer team scored. Her tally shows two crossed groups of 5 and 3 single marks. She draws one ball picture for each goal. How many ball pictures does she draw?
questions.explain: 5 and 5 make 10, and 3 more marks make 13 goals, so 13 ball pictures. Each crossed group holds 5 marks, not 4.

questions.question: Owen has a list of 9 muffins he baked. He wants to make a picture graph. Which is the right way to draw it?
options: Draw one muffin picture for each muffin.
Draw two muffin pictures for one muffin.
Draw one muffin picture for the whole list.
Draw one muffin picture for two muffins.
questions.explain: A picture graph like this is one-to-one: one muffin, one picture, so a list of 9 gives 9 pictures. Two muffins in one picture makes the row too short.

questions.question: A class table shows the weather in May: 7 rainy days and 10 sunny days. Jo draws one picture for each day. How many pictures go in the rainy row?
questions.explain: The rainy row uses the rainy number, 7 days, so it needs 7 pictures. The 10 belongs to the sunny row.

questions.question: Maya tallied the birds at the feeder: one crossed group of 5 and 4 single marks. Later she saw 2 more birds. She draws one bird picture for each bird. How many bird pictures does she draw?
questions.explain: The tally is 5 and 4, which is 9 birds, and 2 more makes 11, so she draws 11 pictures. Do not forget the 2 new birds or count the crossed group as 4.

questions.question: Ravi's tally shows two crossed groups of 5 dogs. He drew 8 dog pictures, one for each dog. What went wrong?
options: He drew one picture for two dogs.
He drew two pictures for one dog.
He drew one picture for each group.
He counted each group of 5 as 4.
questions.explain: Two crossed groups are 5 and 5, so there are 10 dogs and 10 pictures. Ravi counted each group as 4, so his row is two pictures short.

questions.question: Room 5's pet tally shows two crossed groups of 5 for cats, and one crossed group of 5 and 2 marks for dogs. Each pet gets one picture. How many pictures do both rows need in all?
questions.explain: Cats are 5 and 5, which is 10 pictures, and dogs are 5 and 2, which is 7; 10 and 7 make 17. Counting a crossed group as 4 gives too few pictures.

questions.question: Nina's reading tally has one crossed group of 5 and some single marks. She drew 8 book pictures, one for each book. How many single marks are in her tally?
questions.explain: The 8 pictures stand for 8 books, and the crossed group is 5, so 3 single marks are left. A crossed group always means 5, never 4.
